Second countability of N is the paper's own setting (ETT.tex:255), so this is not an added hypothesis relative to the paper. (2) IsCauchyEmbedding.isCauchySurfaceOn_inf_of_secondCountable concludes D.IsCauchySurfaceOn (A ⊓ B) (φ '' S) for every Cauchy surface S of M, with no hDac and no hDext. That is ETT.tex:1941's 'φ(Σ) is a Cauchy surface of A∩B' at full strength; the scaffold's isCauchySurfaceOn_inf follows from it in one term. (3) Causality.isCauchySurfaceOn_inf_of_secondCountable (abstract: C causal, T Cauchy in M, in A and in B, M T2 and second countable) asks no causal arc-connectedness and no morphism. (4) isCauchyInclusion_inf_of_secondCountable adds hDac, used only for the global hyperbolicity of A ⊓ B (through inf_causallyConvexIn_of_secondCountable). This is disclosed as ⚠ strengthened in the checklist and in REPORT.hypotheses. (5) c_ext_connexe_of_secondCountable is the scaffold's c_ext_connexe without hDac, hDext and hthrough, with [SecondCountableTopology N] added; it names the splitting ψ (disclosed, ⚠ strengthened). Its statement is identical to the strict library's c_ext_connexe'_of_secondCountable (finding 4). The library's hypothesis-free c_ext_connexe_of_connectedSpace_of_secondCountable implies it. No statement is quietly weakened (kb/0011); every hypothesis beyond the paper is disclosed and the row is partial. Witness timelikeLine_gateArc_cauchy_inf: a Cauchy embedding gateArc that is not onto, with A = range gateArc and B = ⊤ given as actual IsCauchyInclusion terms. So the hypotheses of the middle step and of the Cauchy inclusion are jointly satisfiable, and the witness is not vacuous. Its A ≤ B, which makes A ⊓ B = A, is disclosed in SCOPE.

checks.findings_of_paper: Citations are right. ETT.tex:1940–1941 hold 'The map M→A∩B is a Cauchy embedding, so φ(Σ) is a Cauchy surface of A∩B'. def:cauchy_embedding_cauchy_extension is at 1858, its sentence at 1859–1861. lem:Cauchy_plongement_toutes is at 1865, and ETT.tex:255 is the topological-spacetime definition. Finding 1 is right. The step is true on T2, second countable spacetimes for any causality: Causality.isCauchySurfaceOn_inf_of_secondCountable needs no morphism, so the paper's φ(Σ), Cauchy in N, A and B by its own lem:Cauchy_plongement_toutes, falls under it. The paper gives no argument. The two cases of the end-point argument are exactly what Lean proves: opposite sides by mem_of_le_of_le_of_subsingleton (N causal, φ(Σ) met at most once by a causal curve of N); the same side by mem_image_or_tendsto_of_above/_below plus t2_separation, with a last value in A∩B contradicting inextensibility and the two limits landing in A∖B and B∖A. Finding 2's substance is right: a Cauchy embedding M→A∩B includes a Cauchy surface of A∩B and the global hyperbolicity of A∩B (ETT.tex:1859), and neither is argued in the proof. Its wording overstates two points (findings 1 and 2 below), and finding 1's suggested wording is incomplete (finding 3 below). The reading of 'M → A∩B is a Cauchy embedding' as IsCauchyInclusion D hφ.rangeOpens (A ⊓ B) is raised in REPORT.questions and not decided. OQ-94 is left open (registers/DECISIONS.md:317, OPEN).

findings.what: Finding 2 says 'the so runs the wrong way … the Cauchy-surface statement is what has to be proved, not a consequence'. The inference itself is valid: if M → A∩B is a Cauchy embedding, φ(Σ) is a Cauchy surface of A∩B for every Σ by lem:Cauchy_plongement_toutes (ETT.tex:1865), which the finding's own parenthesis cites. The defect is that the premise is asserted without argument, and establishing it means proving that a Cauchy surface of M goes onto one of A∩B. The sentence is circular as a proof; it is not an invalid inference. Sent as worded, it would tell the author that a valid deduction is invalid.
findings.fix: Reword: 'ETT.tex:1940: the premise "M → A∩B is a Cauchy embedding" is asserted, not argued. By def:cauchy_embedding_cauchy_extension (ETT.tex:1858–1861) it contains the conclusion (some Cauchy surface of M carried onto one of A∩B; then every one, lem:Cauchy_plongement_toutes) and the global hyperbolicity of A∩B. So the sentence is circular: φ(Σ) being Cauchy in A∩B is what must be proved.'

findings.what: Finding 2's 'The global hyperbolicity of A∩B is not argued either: here it comes from the causal convexity of A∩B in N, with N causally arc-connected' leaves out two facts. First, the paper has its own route: theo:geroch_sing (ETT.tex:1771–1777, (iii)⇒(i)) gives global hyperbolicity from a Cauchy surface on singular flat spacetimes, once the Cauchy-surface half is shown. The caveat is that def:singular_spacetime (ETT.tex:1502) asks connectedness, which for A∩B is the lemma's conclusion. Second, the conclusion of lem:C_ext_connexe does not use the global-hyperbolicity half at all (c_ext_connexe_of_isCauchySurfaceOn takes only the Cauchy surface). Without these, the author reads a gap that needs a new ingredient.
findings.fix: Add: 'In the paper's setting theo:geroch_sing (iii)⇒(i) would give it from the Cauchy surface (modulo the connectedness that def:singular_spacetime, ETT.tex:1502, asks of A∩B); the lemma's conclusion does not need it.'

findings.what: Finding 1's suggested wording for the author, '…if none meets it on the curve, both leave A∩B through its end point, which would lie in (A∖B)∩(B∖A)', covers only the same-side case. When γ_A meets φ(Σ) after c and γ_B before it (the opposite-sides case the finding's own body treats, case (d)), the two curves do not leave A∩B through one end point. There the contradiction comes from N causal and φ(Σ) meeting a causal curve of N at most once. As a proposed replacement text it is an incomplete proof.
findings.fix: Add the clause: '…; if they meet it on opposite sides of the curve, a piece of each joins into a causal curve of N that meets φ(Σ) twice unless the curve itself meets it.'

findings.what: IsCauchyEmbedding.c_ext_connexe_of_secondCountable has exactly the statement of the strict library's Causal.IsCauchyEmbedding.c_ext_connexe'_of_secondCountable (Causal/CExtConnexeSecondCountable.lean:189). `type_of% @…c_ext_connexe'_of_secondCountable.{u,v} = type_of% @…c_ext_connexe_of_secondCountable.{u,v}` holds by `with_reducible rfl`. The docstring (:508–512), the module docstring item 3 (:54–57) and REPORT ('the paper's whole route') compare it only with the scaffold's c_ext_connexe and with c_ext_connexe_of_connectedSpace_of_secondCountable, and never say that the same statement is already proved. Graduated as is, the strict library would carry two theorems with one statement. The new one's only added value is its proof, which goes through the middle step.
findings.fix: Say in the declaration docstring and in REPORT that the statement is c_ext_connexe'_of_secondCountable's and that what is new is the proof by the paper's route (φ(Σ) Cauchy in A∩B). Or let the master drop it at graduation in favour of the existing name.
